page: Vultr vx1-g-8c-32g-480s is a general-purpose cloud compute instance configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock of 2.0 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with multithreading enabled, the instance includes 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. It incorporates vector instruction extensions including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, alongside hardware cryptographic acceleration. The hardware configuration delivers 32.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, and includes 480 GB of attached local NVMe SSD storage with a single complimentary public IPv4 address. No discrete GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark testing indicates exceptional single-threaded execution capabilities balanced by mid-range multi-core scaling. In synthetic compute evaluations, stress-ng single-core performance reached top-tier status at 3,620.38, mirrored by top-tier single-threaded gzip compression at 39.86 GB/s and bzip3 decompression at 17.74 GB/s. Geekbench text processing also achieved top-decile performance at 3,042 points. Multi-core operations landed consistently in the median tier across Geekbench (7,763 points), PassMark CPU testing (18,511.27 points), and multi-threaded decompression. Memory throughput measured 71.66 GB/s for large uncached reads and 41.2 GB/s for writes. Real-world application throughput tests showed steady median results, generating 15.69 million Redis SET operations per second and 26.38 GB/s in static web serving. While lightweight LLM text generation achieved top-tier performance at 403.74 tokens per second on a 135M model, prompt processing throughput degraded to the lower quartile on larger 7B parameter models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides high compute density and reliable performance stability without the unpredictable contention typical of shared-core instances. The integrated 480 GB NVMe storage eliminates separate block volume attachment costs for I/O-intensive services. However, the 2.0 GHz base clock speed and four physical core topology constrain dense parallel compiling and memory-heavy machine learning workflows. As a result, the instance is appropriate for relational and key-value databases, medium-scale web application serving, backend microservices, caching layers, and continuous integration pipelines.
description: Vultr vx1-g-8c-32g-480s is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 8 dedicated AMD EPYC vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores operating at 2.0 GHz, 32.0 GB of memory, and 480 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The x86_64 processor supports AVX-512 and cryptographic extensions, showing top-tier single-threaded compute, data compression, and text parsing in benchmark evaluations. Multi-threaded throughput, PassMark scores, and memory bandwidth fall squarely into median performance brackets, accompanied by solid throughput in Redis operations and static web delivery. With its balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio and bundled high-speed local disk, the instance presents dependable resource allocation without shared-core interference. It is well matched for mid-sized database management, backend web serving, enterprise application hosting, and CI/CD automation pipelines that require dedicated CPU execution without discrete GPU acceleration.
